claims.text: The starting nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 has a homogeneous solute distribution and no pre-existing precipitates.
A single-step tailored anneal can nucleate and grow a controlled population of coherent nanoprecipitates in W38Ta36Cr15V11.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation is an established design strategy for tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The preformed coherent nanoprecipitates will remain stable and controlled during irradiation to approximately 8 dpa.
Preformed coherent nanoprecipitates will prevent further radiation-induced precipitation in W38Ta36Cr15V11 up to approximately 8 dpa.
The intervention will maintain negligible irradiation hardening.
The annealing intervention will improve the alloy's suitability for practical bulk fabrication.
The deliberately formed nanoprecipitates will sequester solute atoms.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Locking solutes into preformed nanoprecipitates will lower the chemical driving force for radiation-induced solute segregation and precipitation.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Improved dislocation transmission and defect-sink behavior will maintain low irradiation hardening.
At approximately 8 dpa, the annealed alloy will exhibit significantly reduced or suppressed radiation-induced precipitate growth relative to the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 8 dpa, the annealed alloy will have a lower irradiation-defect density than the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 8 dpa, the annealed alloy will show similar or lower irradiation hardening than the unmodified alloy.
Unmodified nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 will develop radiation-induced precipitation.
Radiation-induced precipitation in the unmodified alloy will be associated with irradiation hardening.
The intervention is effective from approximately 300 to 600 degrees Celsius and up to approximately 8 dpa.
Outside the proposed temperature or dose window, accelerated precipitate evolution or coarsening may compromise the intervention's benefit.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as a single-step annealing treatment while simultaneously being characterized as following a stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation approach; the relationship between a single processing step and the stated stepwise process is not resolved.

The hypothesis frames irradiation hardening as negligible and to be retained, whereas the baseline says the unmodified alloy develops precipitation-associated hardening. The predicted outcome only requires similar or lower hardening than that baseline, leaving the baseline hardening level internally ambiguous.
